grade.rationale: The implementation is thoughtfully structured and supports dependency injection, deterministic ordering, containment checks, and bounded evidence. However, several valid SARIF constructs are interpreted incorrectly, suppressed results are emitted as active findings, and some malformed reports escape the intended unavailable-result error path.

summary: The sensor has a solid overall design, but SARIF URI decoding, tool-component resolution, suppression handling, exception normalization, and command tokenization need correction. The supplied build evidence reports no findings; ESLint was unavailable because its local module was missing. Test coverage is unknown.

grade.rationale: Valid encoded artifact URIs and name-only tool-component references can be resolved incorrectly, accepted suppressions are treated as active findings, and explicit empty command arguments are lost.

Responsibilities are divided into focused helpers and immutable records, although the custom command parser and URI-resolution logic duplicate subtle platform and standards behavior that is difficult to maintain safely.
Naming and control flow are generally clear, but assumptions about SARIF suppression semantics, URI decoding order, and the supported command-line quoting dialect are not documented.
Common JSON, I/O, and data errors are converted into unavailable results, but URI and path-processing exceptions can still fault RunAsync instead of following that contract.
The injected command runner and public stream-based parser make the main behavior straightforward to test. Coverage is unknown, and the edge cases identified here warrant focused tests.

findings.title: Accepted SARIF suppressions are emitted as active findings
findings.description: The result filter excludes only kind values pass and notApplicable. A failing result whose suppressions array contains an accepted suppression is therefore mapped into a normal ReviewFinding, even though the SARIF producer or user has explicitly suppressed it. This can reintroduce waived diagnostics and distort review results.
findings.recommendation: Inspect result.suppressions before mapping the result and omit results with an accepted suppression, or expose a clearly documented option to include suppressed results while preserving their suppression state.

findings.title: Name-only tool-component references resolve against the driver
findings.description: SARIF toolComponent references can identify an extension by name without supplying an index. The implementation ignores the name and converts a missing index into component zero, which represents the driver in the local component list. The result can consequently inherit the wrong rule title, severity, help text, and properties.
findings.recommendation: Represent components with their tool-component identity and resolve toolComponent by index when present, otherwise by its name or GUID. Validate that multiple supplied identifiers refer to the same component.

findings.title: Artifact URIs are decoded before URI resolution
findings.description: ResolvePath percent-decodes the entire URI reference before parsing or combining it with a base URI. Encoded reserved characters then acquire URI syntax: for example, foo%23bar.cs becomes foo#bar.cs, so resolution against a file base treats bar.cs as a fragment and maps the finding to foo. Encoded slashes and question marks can similarly change path structure or query handling.
findings.recommendation: Normalize separators without decoding reserved characters, resolve the original escaped URI reference against its base, and obtain the decoded filesystem path from the resulting file URI. Decode individual path components only when handling a non-URI filesystem representation.

findings.title: URI and path errors can escape the unavailable-result contract
findings.description: The report-ingestion catch filter handles JSON, I/O, invalid-data, and invalid-operation exceptions, but location resolution can also throw UriFormatException, ArgumentException, or NotSupportedException while unescaping, constructing URIs, or normalizing paths. Such a report faults RunAsync instead of returning a SensorScanResult marked unavailable like other invalid reports.
findings.recommendation: Catch the expected URI and path-format exception types around parsing and convert them to the same unavailable result. Prefer wrapping per-report structural failures in InvalidDataException so callers see one consistent failure contract.

findings.title: The command splitter drops explicitly empty arguments
findings.description: Quote characters change parser state but do not mark a token as present, and tokens are emitted only when the buffer contains characters. Consequently, commands containing "" or '' lose that argument entirely. This changes positional arguments for analyzers that require an explicit empty value.
findings.recommendation: Track whether a token has started independently from the buffer length, and emit the token when whitespace or end-of-input is reached even when its quoted content is empty. Add tests for empty quoted arguments, adjacent quoted segments, whitespace, and escaped quotes.
